flange_on_bark:shoulder.reading_note: the consistent adverse end — the Zone-1 fit slipped

zone3_fit:shoulder.reading_note: intermediate — the Zone-3 fit held while the Zone-1 fit slipped

bark_bearing.before_anode_bond: unpriced — before ingrowth the deep tie is not the anode but the sleeve's grip in the Ø15 channel and ice in the 2 mm gap at the cold edge, which 103 leaves unbounded (zone3_fit.share.state1_ties_not_bounded)
bark_bearing.reading: U = (1/k_A + 1/k_s)/(1/k_A + 1/k_s + 1/k_F) on 103's stiffnesses, premise (b), sway and slow (relaxed PEEK): the fraction of a radial change of the bark the flange follows, so the reading loses it (our reading of a growth push as a displacement source; k_F is the air-dry bark readings, green bark is softer); U is priced with the anode BONDED (103's state 2) — before ingrowth the deep tie is a grip 103 leaves unbounded, so U there is not priced; under premise (a) a rising bark can lift the flange off the sleeve — our reading, 103 does not model lift-off

design_terms: (α_s − α_w)·z_t + (α_s − α_h)·h — nulled in the base reading; each ppm/K of mismatch costs z_t (or h) in mm × 1e-3 µm/K, and α_s = α_w cannot be designed while α_w is one reading

scale_thickness_knob.reference: the t 2 mm row of the base table at the same gap
scale_thickness_knob.reading: each row is the base table's row at a thicker scale, computed by the same function; the field the offset term needs at the sensor depends on the period alone, so a longer best period also raises it — `within_sensor_linear_range` gives the best period the sensor's linear range allows and the remanence needed there. The base table's population stays t 1–2 mm.

unwrap.basis_note: season-consistent: winter = the frost swing with no growth; growing season = a month of the fast end's increment (laid down over ≥ 4 months — our assumption; a growing-season outage of a month is itself an assumption, 110's outages fall in winter) plus the daily swing; cross-season = an outage spanning both. P/2 bounds an absolute-in-period phase; the collector's «half a pole» bounds an incremental pole counter, a different reader. A period above P* buys unwrap margin at a small cost to the OFFSET term (its optimum is flat) — the angle and mismatch errors grow in proportion to P.
unwrap.count_home: the server unwraps the delivered phases — nothing persisted on the device (03_01: the RTC backup domain does not survive an outage on our board). What breaks it: a maintenance event that moves the sensor against the scale (radome off/on, a board re-seat) — a step the server must mark as a discontinuity; a ledger whose old readings are archived or expire — the server keeps a persisted running unwrapped position, not a recompute over history; creep of the sensor's mount; and the phase needs a field on the wire.
